novel_features.name: Home delivery-fee board
novel_features.description: Rank every restaurant near your saved home address by what delivery actually costs you.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining your authenticated saved address to a full-area vendor sweep; the web UI shows fees one card at a time and can never rank a whole city.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the question is 'what is cheapest to get delivered to me', not 'what is this one restaurant's fee'.

novel_features.name: Cross-restaurant dish search
novel_features.description: Find which nearby restaurant sells a specific dish cheapest, searching every synced menu at once.
novel_features.rationale: Requires full-text search across every product of every synced vendor; the API only ever returns one vendor's menu per call, so no foodpanda surface can answer this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for item-level price hunting; use search when you want restaurants by name instead.

novel_features.name: Menu and price drift
novel_features.description: Show what changed in a restaurant's menu and prices between two syncs.
novel_features.rationale: Requires historical menu snapshots in the local store; the API is stateless and exposes no price history at all.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to catch price rises, removed items, or newly added deals over time.

novel_features.name: Commercial posture signals
novel_features.description: Rank vendors by advertising and placement signals: CPC ad participation, promoted and premium status, and ranking score.
novel_features.rationale: Requires reading ncr_pricing_model, is_promoted, premium_position and vendor_points across an entire area at once; no foodpanda surface aggregates these.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for competitive analysis of who buys placement. It does not report merchant commission rates, which are not exposed in any consumer surface.

novel_features.name: Delivery coverage test
novel_features.description: Determine which vendors actually deliver to an arbitrary point using each vendor's published delivery radius.
novel_features.rationale: Requires per-vendor delivery radius joined against a target coordinate; nothing on the site answers 'does this place reach my office'.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before assuming a restaurant is orderable from an address you have not tried.

novel_features.name: True cost fee board
novel_features.description: Compare the full cost structure across an area: delivery fee, minimum order, service fee and VAT together.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a local join across four separate fee fields for every vendor in an area; the site surfaces only the headline delivery fee per card.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when headline delivery fee is misleading because service fee or minimum order dominates.

novel_features.name: Review topic breakdown
novel_features.description: Split a restaurant's blended star rating into per-topic scores so food quality and delivery quality are separated.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregating per-topic scores across paginated reviews; the site collapses everything into one star value.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to tell 'the food is bad' apart from 'the delivery is bad' before trusting a rating.

novel_features.name: Cross-market comparison
novel_features.description: Run the same query across every foodpanda market and compare vendor counts, ratings and fees side by side.
novel_features.rationale: Requires fanning one query across multiple country backends and normalizing the results into a single local table.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for regional benchmarking; use vendors list when you only care about one city.

novel_features.name: Live search with match confidence
novel_features.description: Search vendors live upstream and label how strongly each result actually matched the query.
novel_features.rationale: foodpanda's search is fuzzy and never returns an empty result set, so weak matches look identical to real ones without local scoring.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this for live upstream search where match quality matters; use 'search' instead for offline full-text search over already-synced data.

narrative.headline: Every foodpanda restaurant, menu and price in a local database — with cross-restaurant dish search, price history and fee comparison the app cannot do.
narrative.value_prop: foodpanda's API hands you one restaurant at a time and forgets everything the moment you close the tab. This CLI mirrors an entire area into SQLite, so you can ask questions foodpanda structurally cannot answer: which restaurant near me sells the cheapest biryani, what changed in this menu since last week, and how delivery fees really compare once service fee and minimum order are counted. Works across every market foodpanda runs, and needs no API key for catalog data.
narrative.auth_narrative: Catalog browsing needs no credentials at all — vendor search, menus, prices, deals and reviews all work anonymously. Only your own account data (saved addresses, and the `home` command that depends on them) needs a session. Run `foodpanda-pp-cli auth login --chrome` to import the `token` cookie from a browser where you are already signed in; the CLI composes it into an Authorization header. There is no API key to request and nothing to paste.

quickstart.comment: confirm the browser header set is intact and the catalog host is reachable
top-rated restaurants near central Lahore, straight from the live listing

quickstart.command: foodpanda-pp-cli sync --resources vendors --global-param latitude=31.5204 --global-param longitude=74.3587 --global-param country=pk
quickstart.comment: mirror the area's vendors into SQLite; latitude, longitude and country are required because every foodpanda query is geo-scoped
cross-restaurant dish search — the thing no foodpanda surface can do
compare true ordering cost, not just headline delivery fee

troubleshoots.symptom: Every request returns HTTP 403 with an 'Access to this page has been denied' page
troubleshoots.fix: PerimeterX is rejecting the request shape. Run `foodpanda-pp-cli doctor` to confirm the browser header set is being sent; a stripped User-Agent is the usual cause.

troubleshoots.symptom: Search returns results that have nothing to do with the query
troubleshoots.fix: foodpanda's search is fuzzy and never returns empty. Use `find --explain` to see match confidence and filter out weak rows.

troubleshoots.symptom: A vendor code returns 404 on the menu command
troubleshoots.fix: Vendor codes are market-scoped. Pass the same --country you used for the listing; a Pakistani code will 404 against the Singapore backend.
Run `foodpanda-pp-cli auth login --chrome` from a browser profile signed in to foodpanda, then retry.

troubleshoots.symptom: Offline commands return nothing after a fresh install
troubleshoots.fix: Run `foodpanda-pp-cli sync --resources vendors --global-param latitude=31.5204 --global-param longitude=74.3587` first; dish and menu-diff also populate menu snapshots as they run.

troubleshoots.symptom: Grocery or pandamart products are missing
troubleshoots.fix: Darkstores are listed but their product catalog is a separate q-commerce surface this CLI does not cover. Restaurant menus are unaffected.

troubleshoots.symptom: `search` fails with 'Invalid or non-existent country: null'
troubleshoots.fix: The framework `search` defaults to --data-source auto and tries the live endpoint, which needs coordinates. Use `search <term> --data-source local` for offline FTS over synced data, or `find <term> --latitude <lat> --longitude <lng>` for live search.
Pass the geo scope explicitly: `sync --resources vendors --global-param latitude=<lat> --global-param longitude=<lng> --global-param country=pk`.

troubleshoots.symptom: Delivery fees all show the same value (e.g. 99 everywhere)
troubleshoots.fix: That is foodpanda's flat listing floor, not a real price. Run `auth login --chrome` so `home` can resolve true per-vendor fees; rows then report fee_source: vendor-detail.

narrative.when_to_use: Reach for this CLI whenever a question spans more than one restaurant, or spans time. It is the right tool for comparing prices, fees or ratings across many vendors at once, for finding which nearby restaurant sells a specific dish, for tracking how a menu changes between syncs, and for pulling structured menu data for analysis. It covers every foodpanda market, not just one country.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to place an order, build a cart, or pay — it is read-only by design and has no checkout.
Do not use it to fetch merchant commission rates; those are contract terms that appear in no consumer-facing foodpanda response.
Do not use it for pandamart or grocery product catalogs; darkstores are listed but their item catalog is a separate surface this CLI does not cover.
Do not use it to read your past orders; foodpanda exposes no web order-history route.
Do not use it for a competitor delivery platform such as Uber Eats, Deliveroo or Careem — it only speaks to foodpanda.
